newsitem.title: CHINA: CATHAY DOWN ON DISAPPOINTING H1 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: CATHAY DOWN ON DISAPPOINTING H1 RESULTS.

text.p: A sharp fall in interim earnings triggered disappointed selling and depressed the price of Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd in Thursday's trading, brokers said.
"The disappointed results triggered selling," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities. "The profit fall was sharper than the market expected."
Cathay shares fell HK$0.60 or 4.29 percent to HK$13.40 in mid-morning on volume of 6.74 million.
Cathay on Wednesday reported a 35.2 percent fall in profit to HK$1.07 billion for the six months to June 30.
Meanwhile, shares of Cathay's 43.97 percent controlling shareholder Swire Pacific Ltd rose ahead of the release of its interim results due later on Thursday.

Swire gained HK$0.75 to HK$75.75 on volume of 1.80 million shares. "Expectations of an encouraging interim earnings growth in view of the recent strong response to sales of flats, and steady income flow from its rental property portfolio aided buying," said a sales manager at a regional brokerage.
